main_text.p: thora & cocochymia, quæ contentorum sunt dispositiones medicæ quæ suis signis manifestantur. Temperamentum corporis, ætas, consuetudo, sexus, evacuatio naturalis suppressa, regio, aër &c. non tantum signa sunt humorum redundantium, sed etiam causa. Plethora est redundantia æqualis omnium humorum in venis contentorum. Interdum solius sanguinis redundantia, plethora dicitur. Est autem duplex, quoad vasa, & quoad vires. Illius signum & causa, est temperamentum calidum humidum, adolescentia, victus plenior, vita jucunda, sanguinis evacuatio suppressa. Signum tantum est color rubeus, habitus carnosus &c. Redundantia ad vires cognoscitur ex corporis gravitate. Cacochymia est redundantia humoris ; a sanguine diversi; melancholiæ scilicet, pilis, pituitæ. Corpus ergo calidum siccum, juventus, æstas, victus calidus & parcus, immodica exercitatio, sicut bilem generant, ita & designant: tum enim facies
[illegible, ~20 letters] marginal notes on the right edge are largely cut off and illegible; not transcribed.

page.notes: The right margin carries very small, faint marginal notes, many cut off at the scan edge and mostly illegible; they are not transcribed. The strip at the far right also shows a neighbouring page edge and show-through, which is excluded. Line-end hyphens in the text, such as "humi-dum" and "cor-poris", are rendered as joined words where the printed hyphen is present. Paragraph division is uncertain: the text may run on across the lines "dicitur" and "Est autem", which I have treated as one paragraph.
